questions.question: Which of our five device lines fund the company and which consume it — revenue, margin, trajectory by line?
questions.verdict_headline: PP3500 and cloud-suite fund the company — 59.7% of trailing-4Q gross margin ($27.0M of the portfolio's $45.2M GM on $88.2M revenue, window 2025-Q3..2026-Q2); all six lines gross-margin positive; margins compressing on IP5000, PP3000

questions.question: How concentrated are we — PCA franchise, top-3 GPOs, single systems — and what does losing one anchor GPO do to the 5-year plan?
questions.verdict_headline: Meridian Health Alliance carries 38.4% of FY2025 direct-book revenue — above the 30% guardrail on the direct-book basis, and basis-sensitive: the direct book covers 50.6% of total FY2025 revenue, and Meridian Health Alliance's floor share of TOTAL revenue is 19.4% (under the guardrail); top-3 accounts 25.5%, PCA franchise 74.5%; losing the anchor GPO dents every plan year by $15.6M (14.9% of the FY2026 plan) under the stated constant-dent scenario

questions.question: What share of revenue is recurring today vs the Y5 plan — and which parts of the $350M target are contracted, modeled, or aspiration?
questions.verdict_headline: Recurring revenue is 10.8% of revenue today (FY2026H1) vs 68.6% planned for FY2030; of the $350.0M target, $128.0M rides on already-cleared products, $12.0M on letter-to-file changes, and $210.0M (60.0%) sits behind FDA decisions not yet received — and within the $240.0M recurring proxy itself, $210.0M (87.5%) is behind those decisions

questions.question: Does the subscription model work at unit level — LTV per connected pump vs cost-to-serve, and is Cloud Suite cannibalizing hardware ASP?
questions.verdict_headline: Unit economics fail the guardrail: LTV per connected pump $2,237 vs $2,720 cost-to-serve over the same 5-year horizon (ratio 0.82 vs the 3.0 floor); 28 of 39 active sites run ARR below cost-to-serve — concentrated in small sites — and the mean hardware discount at subscribed sites is 5.8% vs the 5% tolerance

questions.question: How much plan revenue sits behind FDA decisions we haven't received — by regulatory dependency, with slip triggers?
questions.verdict_headline: $366.0M of the $1,000.0M five-year plan sits behind FDA decisions not yet received; exposure crosses the 40% threshold in FY2029, FY2030 (peak 60.0% in FY2030)

questions.question: Is the concept pipeline converting, and how does our clearance cycle time compare with our own history and with BD/Baxter?
questions.verdict_headline: Competitor 510(k) review runs a median 213 days received→decision across 29 infusion-pump clearances since 2021; fastest frequent filer is Baxter Healthcare Corporation at 74 days median

questions.question: What is our actual share of the US PCA/smart-pump segment — taking share from BD/Baxter or growing with the market?
questions.verdict_headline: US (NA-proxy) PCA/LVP smart-pump share is a RANGE, not a number: ~0.029%–0.047% of installed base and ~0.55%–1.1% of annual segment dollars (A-003 denominator, LOW confidence); our installed base grew ~16.0%/yr vs the assumed market ~7.3%/yr — directionally gaining, from a tiny base (mismatched bases: ours is UNIT growth of our NA in-segment book; A-003's rate is the DOLLAR CAGR of the total US infusion-pump market — directional comparison only)

questions.question: What are we winning and losing on — and how many recent losses cite predictive monitoring we don't have?
questions.verdict_headline: Trailing-365d win rate is 50.7% of decided opportunities (37 won / 36 lost; 10 no-decision excluded) vs the 50% stand-in target; dollar-weighted we win 42.9% of decided CRM value ($23,682,000 won vs $31,550,000 lost — we lose bigger deals than we win); 11 of 36 losses (30.6%) have the predictive-monitoring gap primary or cited — $9,961,000 in CRM value

questions.question: Are we winning displaced accounts where an incumbent has an open recall or integration disruption — and how long does the window stay open?
questions.verdict_headline: Method demo (fabricated CRM joined to REAL FDA recall dates): we win 53.7% of decided opportunities where the incumbent had an FRN recall posted within 180 days of close (n=54) vs 22.2% outside the window (n=9); the 0-3 months bucket wins at the highest rate (56.2%) while the interior buckets are flat (~50.0%) — not a smooth decay; the >12 months / no prior recall tail is far lower (14.3%, n=7 — small n)

questions.question: Where do we sit vs Alaris/Spectrum IQ/Plum 360 on 5-year TCO per pump — the buyer's spreadsheet?
questions.verdict_headline: Indicative, assumption-bounded: our 5-yr TCO is $8,900/pump all-in ($5,100 on the capital+service basis) vs a class-wide competitor range of ~$3,000–$15,000 on capital+service ONLY — competitor consumables and software subscription are undisclosed and excluded, so their true all-in TCO sits ABOVE that range; the ranges overlap and no hard we-win claim is supportable

questions.question: Where are pumps sold but underused — accounts whose utilization/telemetry diverges from what they bought?
questions.verdict_headline: 6 connected site(s) ran below 60% of expected infusion hours over 2026-05..2026-07 (worst 34.0%); 2 clear the ≥10-connected-device materiality bar (S-NA-22, S-EMEA-02); the account-revenue tie the question asks for is blocked — no site→account key exists in any pinned dataset

questions.question: What did competitors clear in the last 90 days, laid against our Y1–Y5 roadmap — anything landing on a feature we scheduled two years out?
questions.verdict_headline: 1 infusion-pump clearance(s) in the 90-day window ending 2026-01-28; 0 flag roadmap-relevant keywords — review against the roadmap lanes

questions.question: How much runway before someone closes the predictive-monitoring gap — is our Y3 timing defensible, and what if an incumbent buys an AI entrant?
questions.verdict_headline: Nobody in the competitive matrix documents predictive monitoring today, but the runway is assumption-thin: a SaMD-only entrant starting at the data anchor (2026-01-28) could clear 2027-07-28 to 2028-01-28 — about 5 months before our F6 2028-H2 launch anchor; an incumbent acquisition inherits the same clock; 0 ai/predictive-flagged clearance(s) in the trailing-12-month watch. The hardware-scenario reassurance is FRAGILE: its fast edge clears the favorable launch anchor by only 27 days and beats an end-of-2028-H2 launch reading by ~5 months — and the H2 anchor refinement is a catalog config choice, not a strategy-doc commitment

questions.question: Where exactly do we sit on PCA feature parity, line by line — which gaps are on the roadmap vs silently unaddressed?
questions.verdict_headline: 10 attributes compared: 2 ahead, 4 parity, 4 behind — 3 behind-gaps have a roadmap lane (of which 2 adjacency-only: integrated_etco2, pca_pause_or_etco2 — the lane responds but does not mechanically close the gap), 1 SILENTLY UNADDRESSED (weight_kg)

questions.question: Is the state-of-the-art analysis still current (EU MDR), and are our headline spec differentiators still ahead?
questions.verdict_headline: ride to scheduled review (2027-04-12): both differentiators remain ahead of every documented competitor value and no refresh trigger fired. Accuracy margin ~6.6x vs best documented competitor on our LAB-basis spec (~4.6x on our volumetric-basis spec — ahead on either basis; competitor cells are nominal/field specs), battery ~2.1x; 0 FRN clearance(s) observed after the SOTA anchor date (2026-04-12) in a snapshot whose coverage ends 2026-01-28

questions.question: For each roadmap feature: documented KOL evidence on file? Which ride on a single voice, and does current sentiment still order the waves?
questions.verdict_headline: META-GAP: all 38 evidence rows are a simulated advisory panel — zero real collected KOL evidence exists (no interviews, surveys, or publications). Within the simulated register: F9 rides on a single voice (E-16.1 floor not met), and the F4, F6, F7, F8 wave slots carry concern-majority sentiment — read as NO documented endorsement of those slots, not as opposition: the register's 3-value vocabulary collapses conditional support into `concern` (stated limitation)

questions.question: Stacked against clearances, KOL data, and attach actuals — which roadmap bet do we kill, and which do we pull forward a year?
questions.verdict_headline: Decision support, not the decision: pull-forward candidate F4 Alerts Engine v1 (smart alarm filtering) (composite 0.616, tie with F6 broken on earliest wave); kill candidate F9 International expansion (EU MDR / Canada) (composite 0.0, tie with F7 broken on weakest evidence base) — sentiment axis is simulated-panel only, demand axis is Cloud attach 84.8%. CAUTION on the kill read: the single F9 voice argues the slot is too LATE and too THIN — a voice FOR earlier EU investment, arithmetically converted into kill support by the 3-value sentiment vocabulary

questions.question: Top three complaint categories this quarter, rate-normalized with a stated denominator — any trending above the risk-file commitment?
questions.verdict_headline: CAPA-review trigger: occlusion-alarm at 3.39 per 100 devices vs threshold 3.0; connectivity at 2.26 per 100 devices vs threshold 2.0 (trailing 90d ending 2026-07-17)

questions.question: How does our adverse-event profile compare to competitors — and what denominator did you use, because MAUDE doesn't have one?
questions.verdict_headline: MAUDE event COUNTS are comparable with caveats; RATE comparison is BLOCKED — the installed-base denominator (A-001) is not yet quantified

questions.question: Any field signal — complaints, near-misses, alarm data — around opioid over-delivery or PCA-by-proxy?
questions.verdict_headline: WATCH TRIGGERED on our internal log (demo-fabricated): 3 over-delivery and 2 PCA-by-proxy-suspected complaint records (2 MDR-filed, 1 under investigation) — E-20.1 zero-tolerance NOT met; the signal→upgrade loop closed for 2 watch-category signals; real class-wide MAUDE context is counts-only (no denominator)

questions.question: What's open on the field-action docket, how timely are our MDRs, and what's the exposure if FDA walks in tomorrow?
questions.verdict_headline: If FDA walks in tomorrow: 2 open docket item(s) (MDR-2026-0005 due in 2 days at the pin date; FSCA-2026-001 rollout incomplete) and 1 late MDR filing(s) in the trailing 12 months — on-time rate 94.7% (18 of 19); E-21.1 NOT met

questions.question: Of last year's field signals, how many landed as design inputs or upgrade-pipeline items — and how many died in a spreadsheet?
questions.verdict_headline: 16 of 40 lifetime signals (40.0%) died in a spreadsheet (no-action or open past the 90-day SLA); trailing 12 months: 6 of 21 (28.6%) died vs 9 landed in design/upgrade — and only 36.8% of adjudicated cohort signals met the SLA, so E-22.1 is NOT met

questions.question: Where do we stand on the current field-update campaign — planned vs actual coverage by region and site, and will we hit the close date?
questions.verdict_headline: Campaign C-2026-02 is 62.7% complete; at current run-rate EMEA, NA will miss the 2026-09-30 close

questions.question: What are our update failure and retry rates — is any hardware rev, firmware baseline, or site profile failing at a rate that says pause and escalate?
questions.verdict_headline: PAUSE TRIGGER: cohort hw B upgrading from 3.1.2 fails on 31.4% of attempted devices (threshold 15.0%) — pause the wave for this cohort and escalate

questions.question: Are customers struggling with this upgrade — tickets per 100 upgraded pumps, rollbacks — and what does an upgrade cost the customer?
questions.verdict_headline: Tickets per 100 attempted upgrades are highest in NA at 21.7; 4 site(s) rolled back; estimated customer-side cost of the on-site portion so far $7,272–$16,412

questions.question: Do we have the capacity to execute the remaining waves on schedule — or do we add headcount, contract labor, or slip?
questions.verdict_headline: Capacity gap to hit the 2026-09-30 close — EMEA, NA STALLED (zero completions in the four weeks to 2026-07-27; EMEA needs 6.4/wk; NA needs 4.7/wk); APAC behind (3.5/wk vs 4.5/wk required); remote conversion covers 0 of 97 on-site-remaining devices today

questions.question: How far behind current is the fleet — % of pumps more than one firmware version behind, at which accounts, and connected vs not?
questions.verdict_headline: 56.7% of the PP3500 fleet is ≥1 firmware version behind (21.9% two behind); connected devices are current at 42.3% vs 44.2% for unconnected

questions.question: Where are we against plan on revenue — by line and region, volume vs price vs timing?
questions.verdict_headline: H1 2026 revenue $46.3M vs plan $48.3M (-4.1%, within the ±5% tolerance overall; 4 of 6 lines breach the band individually on the downside); under plan: cloud-suite -16.4%, SP6500 -15.7%, SP6000 -9.1%, PP3500 -6.3%; masked by IP5000 +24.3%, PP3000 +16.1%; 2026-Q2 alone breached at -5.5%

questions.question: Is the Cloud Suite attach-rate stage-gate holding — the gate that releases the $24M predictive-monitoring spend?
questions.verdict_headline: The attach stage-gate HOLDS at the stand-in level: 43.0% of the PP3500 installed base (295 of 686 pumps) vs the 40% gate — but the $24M releases on a gate NUMBER nobody has ratified; the strategy of record says 'traction' and sets no threshold — and the verdict is denominator-definition-sensitive: under a whole-PCA denominator (884 pumps incl. 198 unconnectable PP3000) attach reads 33.4%, BELOW the stand-in gate; the metric definition is as unratified as the gate number

questions.question: What's our fully-loaded cost per update, remote vs on-site — and the business case for a remote-first campaign at the top non-connected accounts?
questions.verdict_headline: A remote update costs $120 vs an on-site update between $193 (labor-time floor) and $950 (full-day ceiling) — remote is 12.6–62.1% of on-site depending on unmeasured travel; a $380 adapter pays back in 0.5–5.2 update campaigns at the top non-connected accounts
